title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. In each phase two blocks at the left end grow by eating a long run of ones (one double cycle proved in Lean); between phases the head works through an irregular region that is not understood. A halt needs a 1 read in state C next to a long run of ones.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 45,689 cells have been visited and 21,011 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.464). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Tape structure
claims.text: In periodic notation the tape at 109 steps is (100)^6706 1 D>0 (101)^468 10 (011)^2 (01)^4857 (101)^3 (01)^2 (101)^3 (01)^2 ...: a long block (100)^n at the growing left end, then blocks of (101) and (01) that the head converts, and further right a long periodic region of (101)^3 (01)^2 units. At 108 steps the left block was (100)^2053.

claims.title: The growth phase
claims.text: 0^inf B> 0 (011)^(n+2) 0 011 011 (01)^(m+1) (01101)^(q+1) 011 111 R reaches 0^inf B> 0 (011)^(n+3) 0 011 011 (01)^(m+4) (01101)^(q+1) 011 R (written as the run re-brackets it) in 10m+20n+20q+204 steps, for all n, m, q and every tape R.

claims.title: Phases
claims.text: The run alternates growth phases, in which the blocks (011)^n and (01)^m at the left end grow by eating a long run of ones three cells per double cycle, with an irregular stretch in which the head works through a list of short words; the runs of ones are made by earlier phases.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Missing: the rule for the irregular region between phases; see Next steps in the README.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 45,689 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Blocks that grow by eating runs of ones
html: At the moments the head is at the left end in state B, the tape often reads

Two blocks, (011)^n and (01)^m, then a middle block, then a long run of ones. Every two cycles the run of ones loses three cells and the blocks grow: n goes up by one and m by three. This is proved in Lean for all sizes.

<svg viewBox='0 0 560 70' role='img' aria-label='two blocks at the left, a middle block, and a run of ones being eaten' style='width:100%;max-width:560px;height:auto;font:12px var(--mono)'><rect x='10' y='15' width='120' height='24' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='70' y='31' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>(011)^n</text><rect x='130' y='15' width='140' height='24' fill='var(--accent)'/><text x='200' y='31' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>(01)^m</text><rect x='270' y='15' width='100' height='24' fill='var(--sunk)' stroke='var(--line-strong)'/><text x='320' y='31' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--fg2)'>(01101)^q</text><rect x='370' y='15' width='170' height='24' fill='none' stroke='var(--head)'/><text x='455' y='31' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--fg2)'>1^r: eaten 3 at a time</text></svg>

When the run of ones is gone, the head works through an irregular list of short words further right, and later a new phase starts with the next long run of ones. That irregular part is not understood, so there is no rule from one phase to the next.

Where it could halt

Only in state C on a 1 with at least six 1s to its left: next to a long run of ones, the very thing the phases eat. Inside a phase this never happens; it would have to happen in the irregular part.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.464). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 45,689 cells (25,401 left of the start, 4,417 right), with a density of 1s of 0.46.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Phases in which two blocks (011)^n (01)^m at the left end grow by eating a long run of ones (proved in Lean), separated by work on an irregular list of short words that is not understood; open.
family: growing blocks eating runs of ones
